# s309 — Fewer git calls per command

A test counts the git subprocesses a command starts; repo and worktree probes are answered once per process, and `verify --landed` stops making one git call per ref tip.

**Findings:** research/go-rewrite-evaluation.md, alternatives 1 and code review 7, 2026-10-15 · **Size:** M · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-16** — Verified: full suite 2217 OK (1 skipped) on the final diff; slicer check passes; mutation checks red for the right reason. vcs.is_repo and the worktree lookup are memoised per resolved root plus discovery env (positive answers only; cleared by TempRepo and tui.View.refresh); verify --landed uses vcs.tips_outside (two log calls, with --decorate-refs so log.excludeDecoration cannot hide tips) instead of one merge-base per tip. Git calls: note is-inside-work-tree 3 -> 1; check with a sibling 8 -> 6; verify --landed with 20 tips: 21 merge-base -> 0, 2 log, show <= 21 (documented bound; the closed allowlist has no multi-blob read). Timings on this worktree, interleaved medians: check 188 -> 179-180 ms, list --json --lean 125-126 -> 120-121 ms; reviewer's independent medians under suite load: check 178 -> 173 ms, list 118 -> 115 ms.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** removing the sibling-collision scan from `check`; lazy imports (its own item); any new entry in `vcs.ALLOWED`.

## Why

The Go rewrite evaluation measured reads at 70-80 ms, `render` at 120 ms and `check` at 170 ms, and found that the variable cost is git subprocesses, not Python. Within one command the same read-only probes run again and again: `vcs.is_repo` (`src/slicer/vcs.py:82`) runs inside `merge_in_progress`, `resolve` and `subjects` as well as on its own, and `_current_worktree` (`src/slicer/vcs.py:305`) runs `rev-parse --show-toplevel` twice per sibling scan. `verify --landed`'s `_done_on_another_tip` (`src/slicer/verify.py:471-489`) runs `is_ancestor`, and possibly `show`, for every ref tip, up to 1000 tips. Nothing tests the count, so it can grow unnoticed.

The two `require_no_merge` calls in `main` (`src/slicer/cli.py:4099` and `src/slicer/cli.py:4111`) look deliberate: the first fails fast before waiting on the lock, the second rechecks while holding it. Keep both; the memoised `is_repo` makes the second cheaper.

## Files

- `src/slicer/vcs.py`: memoise `is_repo` and `_current_worktree` per resolved root for the life of the process (a module-level dict, with a function the tests call to clear it). Answers that can change within one command (`MERGE_HEAD`, HEAD) are not cached.
- `src/slicer/verify.py`, `_done_on_another_tip`: fewer calls per tip within the closed allowlist, for example one `log`/`rev-list`-style listing of the tips not in `commit`'s history instead of one `merge-base --is-ancestor` per tip, if an allowed form does it; otherwise a documented bound. No new git command or form without the owner's approval.
- `tests/support.py`: a helper that counts calls to `vcs._run` and clears the memo between tests.
- A new `tests/test_git_calls.py` pinning counts for `check`, one mutating command (`note`) and `verify --landed` on a small fixture.
- `CHANGELOG.md` under Changed (performance).

## Failing tests

- `test_Check_InRepoWithSibling_GitCallsBounded`: `check` in a fixture with one sibling worktree starts at most N git calls (N set from the memoised implementation and recorded in the test).
- `test_Note_InRepo_IsRepoProbedOnce`: a `note` runs `rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` once.
- `test_VerifyLanded_ManyTips_CallsDoNotScalePerTip`: with 20 extra branches, `verify --landed` starts fewer than 20 `merge-base` calls, or the slice records the bound it chose.

## Implement

1. Add the counter helper; write the tests and record today's counts (red against the targets).
2. Memoise the probes; reduce the per-tip calls.
3. CHANGELOG; mutation-check (drop the memo; restore the per-tip loop).
